question: Under the Bolam test as modified by Bolitho, a doctor is NOT negligent if their practice was:

answers.text: Endorsed by any single qualified colleague who would testify in court on their behalf

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A solitary supportive colleague does not satisfy the Bolam test. The standard requires a responsible body of medical opinion — a recognised body of practitioners would have acted similarly.

answers.text: Supported by a responsible body of medical opinion, AND that opinion withstands logical scrutiny (Bolitho modification)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Bolam establishes the 'responsible body of medical opinion' standard. Bolitho adds that the supporting opinion must be logically defensible — the court is not bound by expert opinion that is not capable of withstanding logical analysis.

answers.text: In accordance with the most up-to-date national clinical guidelines at the time of treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Partially correct in principle but not the legal test. Guideline compliance is relevant evidence but does not automatically satisfy Bolam — the standard is a responsible body of opinion, not strict guideline adherence.

answers.text: Taken in good faith under emergency circumstances, regardless of the outcome

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Good faith and emergency circumstances are factors in assessing the standard of care and may affect culpability, but they do not replace the Bolam + Bolitho standard.

overallFeedback.feedback: The standard is Bolam (responsible body of medical opinion) + Bolitho modification (the opinion must withstand logical scrutiny). Courts can reject illogical expert opinion.
Correct. Bolam = responsible body of medical opinion. Bolitho = that opinion must be logically defensible. Both elements must be satisfied.
